issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (Takata recall)
issues.sym: There is usually no warning at all. The danger shows up only in a crash, when the passenger front airbag deploys.
issues.why: These cars got Takata passenger airbag inflators, including some interim replacement parts. The propellant breaks down after years of heat and humidity, and the inflator can burst and throw metal pieces at the people in front.
issues.next: Run your VIN through Nissan/Infiniti's recall lookup or NHTSA today. The new inflator is free at any Infiniti dealer. Until it is replaced, keep anyone out of the front passenger seat; Nissan has told owners of unrepaired older cars not to drive them.

issues.t: Crank or cam sensor can make the engine stall (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, hard starting or no start, low power, or the engine suddenly shutting off while driving.
issues.why: Poor solder joints on the circuit board inside the crankshaft and camshaft position sensors can lose contact, so the computer loses track of engine position.
issues.next: If it stalls, get safely off the road. Ask an Infiniti dealer to check your VIN; the recall replaced the crank sensor and cam sensors free. If the recall was done long ago and symptoms return, have the sensors tested.

issues.t: Ignition coils fail and cause misfires
issues.sym: Rough idle, shaking or stumbling when you accelerate, and a check engine light that may flash. It often gets worse when the engine is warm or the air is damp.
issues.why: The 3.0L V6 uses one coil sitting on top of each spark plug. With age and heat, the coils crack or weaken internally and stop firing their cylinder reliably. Low-quality replacement coils can cause the same misfire codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read to find which cylinder is misfiring, and replace that coil with a good-quality part. Don't drive long with a flashing check engine light; it can overheat the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Long cranking or hard starting, often when warm
issues.sym: The engine turns over for a long time before it catches, or won't start at all, often after a short stop or when the engine is warm.
issues.why: Owners trace this to several worn parts that fail with age on the 3.0L V6: crankshaft or camshaft position sensors, ignition coils, the fuel pump relay, a weak starter, or corroded battery and engine ground cables.
issues.next: Note when it happens (hot, cold, after sitting) and have a shop check sensor signals, fuel pressure and spark while the problem is present. Cleaning battery and ground connections is a simple first step.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption or oil sludge
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, the low-oil light comes on, blue smoke from the exhaust, or in bad cases a knocking engine that fails.
issues.why: Owners of the 3.5L I35 report engines that burn oil and, when oil changes are stretched or the level runs low, sludge that starves the engine. Some owners also link heavy oil use to a front catalytic converter that has broken apart.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every few fill-ups and top up as needed. Keep oil changes on time. If it's burning more than about a quart every 1,000 miles, have a compression and catalytic converter check done before the engine is damaged.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle or tapping noise
issues.sym: A rattle, whine or tapping from the front of the engine, often loudest on cold starts or at certain engine speeds.
issues.why: The timing chain's plastic guides and tensioner wear on the 3.5L V6, letting the chain run loose and slap.
issues.next: Have a shop listen to it and check for timing-related codes. A worn chain can skip a tooth and damage the engine, so don't ignore a noise that keeps getting louder.

issues.t: Catalytic converter fails
issues.sym: Check engine light (often code P0420), a rattle from under the car, a sulfur smell, sluggish acceleration, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: The converters on these V6 cars wear out at higher mileage, and misfires or oil burning speed that up. Failing oxygen sensors can also trigger the same code.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed and the oxygen sensors checked first. If the converter is clogged or broken inside, replace it, and fix any misfire or oil burning so the new one lasts.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts cause vibration and clunks
issues.sym: Strong vibration at idle in Drive, a clunk when you shift or step on the gas, and the engine visibly rocking.
issues.why: The fluid-filled and rubber engine mounts break down with age and heat. Motor mounts are one of the most-reported repairs on these cars.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected with the engine running in gear. Replace broken mounts before the extra movement strains hoses, exhaust parts and axles.

issues.t: Radiator cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant puddles under the front, a sweet smell, the low-coolant level dropping, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The radiator has plastic end tanks that crack with age. The radiator is the most-reported repair on these cars in owner surveys.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it climbs toward hot. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and replace the radiator and any soft hoses together.

issues.t: Power steering hose leaks
issues.sym: Reddish fluid under the front of the car, a whining noise when turning, or steering that feels heavier at low speeds.
issues.why: The high-pressure power steering hose and its crimped fittings harden and seep with age. Some owners also see small leaks at the steering rack.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and top it up. Have the leak traced; a hose is usually a modest repair, but running the pump low on fluid can ruin it.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: Battery or charge warning light, dim or flickering lights, a dead battery, or the car dying while driving.
issues.why: The alternator wears out with mileage. It is one of the more common electrical repairs reported by owners of these cars.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested at a parts store or shop. If the alternator output is low, replace it before you get stranded.

issues.t: Knock sensor code and check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light with a knock sensor code, sometimes with weaker acceleration. Some owners also hear knocking under load.
issues.why: The knock sensor sits under the intake manifold where heat and age wear out the sensor or its wiring. When it fails, the computer may hold back ignition timing to protect the engine.
issues.next: Use premium fuel as Infiniti recommends and have the code confirmed. Replacing the sensor means removing the intake manifold, so it is mostly labor.

issues.t: Mass airflow sensor failure
issues.sym: Hesitation, stalling, rough running, poor fuel mileage, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The mass airflow sensor measures air going into the engine. When it gets dirty or fails, the engine gets the wrong amount of fuel.
issues.next: Have the codes and sensor readings checked. Cleaning the sensor with MAF cleaner sometimes helps; replace it if readings stay off.

issues.t: Check engine light from EVAP valve or leak
issues.sym: Check engine light with an evaporative emissions code. On some I35s owners report stalling, especially right after filling up.
issues.why: The EVAP system traps fuel vapor. Its purge and vent valves fail with age, or small leaks develop, and a stuck-open purge valve can flood the engine with vapor.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks tight first. If the light returns, have the EVAP system smoke-tested and the purge and vent valves checked.

issues.t: Rough or surging idle and stalling
issues.sym: Idle speed hunts up and down, the engine stalls when you come to a stop, or it idles roughly.
issues.why: Carbon builds up in the throttle body and idle air control valve. On the later electronic throttle cars, some owners needed a new throttle body.
issues.next: Have the throttle body and idle air control valve cleaned, then the idle relearn done. If it continues, check for vacuum leaks or a failing throttle body.

issues.t: Clunk or click from the front when turning
issues.sym: A clunk, click or knock from the front end when turning, going over bumps, or turning the wheel at low speed.
issues.why: Worn front struts, strut top mounts and sway bar end links are the usual causes on these cars at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replacing struts with their mounts as complete assemblies is the common fix; get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Front lower control arm pin can break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end and steering that feels odd or pulls.
issues.why: The pin at the frame end of the front lower control arm (transverse link) could break, which affects steering control.
issues.next: Ask an Infiniti dealer to check your VIN. The fix was new left and right control arms, free.

issues.t: Gas pedal can over-travel and limit engine speed (recall)
issues.sym: Pressing the gas pedal hard to the floor can make the engine lose power instead of accelerating.
issues.why: On the electronic throttle, the pedal stopper could let the pedal travel too far under heavy force, which the system read as a fault and limited engine speed.
issues.next: Ask an Infiniti dealer to check your VIN. The repair was a new pedal stopper, free.

issues.t: Oxygen sensors fail
issues.sym: Check engine light, worse fuel mileage, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors wear out over time, and on high-mileage cars they are a common emissions repair.
issues.next: Have the codes read to see which sensor failed. Replace it before it hurts mileage or damages the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve cover or oil pan gaskets
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, burning-oil smell after driving, or oil on the spark plug tubes causing misfires.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gaskets, spark plug tube seals and oil pan gasket harden with age and start to seep.
issues.next: Have the leak located. Fix a valve cover leak early, since oil in the plug wells can ruin ignition coils.

issues.t: CV axle clicks when turning
issues.sym: Clicking or popping when turning sharply, or vibration when accelerating; grease sprayed inside the wheel.
issues.why: The rubber boots on the front axles crack, the grease leaks out, and the constant-velocity joint wears.
issues.next: Have the boots checked at each oil change. A torn boot caught early can be replaced; a noisy joint usually means a new axle.

issues.t: Brake caliper sticks
issues.sym: The car pulls to one side, a burning smell or hot wheel after driving, or uneven brake pad wear.
issues.why: Brake calipers on these older cars corrode and their pistons or slide pins stick, so a pad drags on the rotor.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. A sticking caliper is usually replaced along with pads, and rotors if they are damaged.

issues.t: Starter clicks or won't crank
issues.sym: A single click or nothing when you turn the key, even with a good battery.
issues.why: The starter motor wears out at high mileage. Owners report starter replacements on both the I30 and I35.
issues.next: Have the battery and cables tested first. If they're good and the starter doesn't spin, it needs replacing.
